_meta.basis: Consolidated (Screener.in); Rs crore unless stated. Company EBITDA includes other income and excludes the share of associates; Screener's operating profit (the model's EBITDA) excludes both.
_meta.note: Fact base for the Piramal Pharma initiation. Every number carries a source and the date it was published; nothing published after 30-Sep-2026 is used (later facts sit in research/updates/later-facts.json).

profile.item: Mumbai-based pharma company demerged from Piramal Enterprises (listed 19-Oct-2022) with three businesses: a global contract development and manufacturing business (CDMO, 'Piramal Pharma Solutions', 15 sites in India, North America and the UK), a complex hospital generics business (CHG, 'Piramal Critical Care': inhalation anaesthetics, intrathecal therapy, injectable pain) and an India consumer healthcare (OTC) business (PCH: Little's, Lacto Calamine, i-pill, Saridon, Polycrol, CIR). It also owns 49% of AbbVie Therapeutics India (ophthalmology JV with AbbVie) and 33.33% of Yapan Bio (vaccines/biologics CDMO).
profile.sites: 17 development and manufacturing facilities incl. one via Yapan Bio: India 9 CDMO (Ahmedabad x2, Pithampur, Dahej, Digwal, Mahad, Turbhe, Ennore, Rabale R&D), North America 4 CDMO (Lexington, Riverview, Sellersville, Aurora) plus Bethlehem (inhalation anaesthesia), UK 2 (Grangemouth ADC, Morpeth)
profile.customers: ~500 CDMO customers; 6,000+ hospitals for CHG; 180,000+ chemists and 13,000+ modern-trade outlets for PCH
profile.src: Q4FY26 investor presentation (28-Apr-2026); AR FY26 (corporate overview); CARE Ratings press release (17-Jul-2026)

fy26.inventoryDestocking: Revenue hit by inventory destocking of one large on-patent commercial product (a migraine drug, per analysts on the Q4 call), slower early-stage order inflows in H1FY26 and softer ex-US inhalation-anaesthesia traction; adjusted for destocking, CDMO grew modestly
fy26.src: Q4FY26 press release and investor presentation (28-Apr-2026); AR FY26 consolidated statements (accounts dated 28-Apr-2026); Q4FY26 earnings call (29-Apr-2026)

lossBridge._note: Why FY26 turned to a loss (FY25 profit Rs91 cr -> FY26 loss Rs326 cr, a Rs417 cr swing), company figures
lossBridge.items: Operations: Screener-basis EBITDA fell Rs523 cr (Rs1,445 cr to Rs922 cr) as CDMO revenue fell Rs532 cr, mostly the destocked high-margin on-patent product, on a fixed cost base (employee costs +4.7%, other expenses +5.8% incl. a Rs41.8 cr fire loss); other income rose Rs78 cr (forex gains and write-backs). Depreciation rose Rs15 cr; interest fell Rs81 cr (rates and refinancing); the share of associates fell Rs16 cr. Tax fell only Rs174 cr because India profits stay taxed while overseas losses earn no credit. Exceptional items -Rs196 cr: impairment of an intangible under development Rs175.8 cr, labour-code gratuity/leave provision Rs26.9 cr, a GBP1.25 mn customer settlement Rs14.8 cr, less a Rs21.4 cr insolvency recovery.
lossBridge.src: Q4FY26 press release (28-Apr-2026); AR FY26 notes 27, 32, 33, 34

callPoints: Guidance maintained for FY27; may be revisited after the September quarter (CFO).
No sales expected this fiscal year from the large on-patent product that was destocked (CEO).
Currency added 'about 9% to 10%' to Q1 growth across businesses (CFO).
Tax rate 'will remain elevated in this financial year'; normalised 24-25% at scale; Q1 tax includes a disallowed overseas R&D credit (CFO).
Capex guidance US$120-135 mn for FY27; US$21 mn spent in Q1; Lexington sterile expansion to complete by end-CY2027.
FY30 goal: 25% EBITDA margin, led by CDMO as overseas utilisation rises; CDMO ~60% of the business, ~48% of CDMO revenue from overseas sites.
Gross margins: overseas sites 75-85%, India 55-65%, blended ~64-65%.
Other income = amortisation of capex grants + reversals of prior-period provisions + forex; Q1 was lifted by provision reversals.
Sellersville (US) received an EIR from the USFDA; zero OAI record maintained.
Kenalog supplies to start in Q2FY27; ex-US sevoflurane gaining share; Chinese competition 'remains'.
Not actively looking for acquisitions; organic and greenfield growth (Angel One, 30-Jul-2026).
q1fy27.src: Q1FY27 press release and investor presentation (29-Jul-2026, BSE/NSE); Q1FY27 earnings call transcript (30-Jul-2026, company website); Angel One news (30-Jul-2026)

guidance.fy27: Revenue growth 'early-to-mid-teens' in rupee terms across each business, EBITDA growing faster than revenue on operating leverage, PAT growing; excludes the destocked on-patent product; H2-weighted with a large Q4; ~6-7 points of growth from the rupee at April levels. Net debt/EBITDA to stay ~3.6x through FY27. Capex US$120-135 mn excl. Kenalog. Tax elevated.
guidance.fy27Src: Q4FY26 earnings call (29-Apr-2026), reaffirmed on the Q1FY27 call (30-Jul-2026)
guidance.fy30: Set at the analyst day of 24-Sep-2024 and reaffirmed in Jul-2026: revenue above US$2 bn (about double FY24), CDMO US$1.2 bn at ~25% EBITDA margin, consolidated EBITDA more than 3x FY24 at ~25% margin, net debt/EBITDA ~1x, high-teens ROCE.
guidance.fy30Src: Business Standard (25-Sep-2024); Medical Dialogues; ICICI Direct Q1FY27 note (30-Jul-2026); Q1FY27 call

accounting.item: Company EBITDA includes other income (FY26 Rs213 cr, ~19% of company EBITDA); write-backs of liabilities (Rs55.7 cr) and forex gains (Rs50.3 cr) were half of FY26 other income.
Exceptional items in FY26 (Rs196 cr net) and recurring-looking charges inside EBITDA: fire loss Rs41.8 cr, write-downs of intangibles under development Rs5.4 cr (Rs50.2 cr in FY25) and CWIP Rs5.5 cr.
Effective tax rate above 100% of PBT in FY26: profits taxed in India while overseas losses carry unrecognised deferred tax assets; a disallowed R&D tax credit in Q1FY27.
Working capital released in FY26 (payables Rs2,479 cr vs Rs1,534 cr; receivables down Rs217 cr) flattered CFO (Rs1,653 cr, 202% of Screener EBITDA); inventory up Rs798 cr to 345 days.
